pins.name: GPIO18
pins.label: GPIO18 (Led Neopixel)
pins.notes:
Onboard 6-pixel WS2812/NeoPixel status bar data line. Confirmed via Pimoroni's own official servo2040.hpp (LED_DATA=18, NUM_LEDS=6), Adafruit CircuitPython's pimoroni_servo2040 board def (NEOPIXEL/LED_DATA=GPIO18, NUM_LEDS=6), and the rp-hal-boards crate this board's own pins_arduino.h cites as its source (Gpio18{name:led_data}). This board's own pins_arduino.h #defines PIN_LED/LED_BUILTIN=18 (implying a single LED) and separately PIN_NEOPIXEL=15 (a real servo channel, no NeoPixel role per any source) — both #define-only and never parsed by this project's static-const-only parser, so neither had any prior effect; this chipGpios entry uses the real, vendor-driver-confirmed GPIO.
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO22
pins.label: GPIO22
pins.notes:
ADC_ADDR_0 — 3-bit analog-multiplexer address select line 0 (selects which of the 6 sensor/voltage/current channels feeds the shared ADC on GPIO29). Dedicated onboard hardware, not general purpose. Confirmed via Pimoroni's servo2040.hpp, CircuitPython pins.c, and rp-hal-boards lib.rs (all three name GPIO22 adc_addr_0).
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO23
pins.label: GPIO23 (Button)
pins.notes:
USER_SW — onboard user button, electrically coupled to the BOOTSEL circuit (shop.pimoroni.com: "BOOT button (the BOOT button can also be used as a user button)"), same design pattern as ../pimoroni_tiny2040 GPIO23. Confirmed via Pimoroni's servo2040.hpp (USER_SW=23), CircuitPython pins.c (USER_SW->GPIO23), and rp-hal-boards lib.rs (Gpio23{name:user_sw}) — this board's own pins_arduino.h `#define USER_SW (22u)` is #define-only (never parsed) and, per those 3 sources, appears to be an upstream numbering error (22 is actually ADC_ADDR_0). digital_output/pwm_output deliberately omitted — no source confirms driving this BOOTSEL-coupled line as an output is safe, matching the ../pimoroni_tiny2040 GPIO23 precedent.
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO29
pins.label: GPIO29
pins.notes:
SHARED_ADC — the multiplexer's single physical ADC output pin (per Pimoroni's servo2040.hpp: "multiplex sensing pin for voltage/current and six sensors"); only meaningful once ADC_ADDR_0/1/2 select a channel, so a plain one-shot analogRead() cannot safely be exposed. This board's own pins_arduino.h already treats this the same way (A3/ADC_SHARED deliberately left undeclared, 31u 'not pinned out' sentinel, per the existing pfodWeb NOTE in that file) — this entry only adds pin-picker visibility, matching the ../bigtreetech_SKR_Pico dedicated-GPIO precedent.
Check if available on board
